addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.
- vercel:deploy: Deploy the current project to Vercel. Pass "prod" or "production" as argument to deploy to production. Default is preview deployment.
- vercel:env: Manage Vercel environment variables. Commands include list, pull, add, remove, and diff. Use to sync environment variables between Vercel and your local development environment.
- vercel:status: Show the status of the current Vercel project — recent deployments, linked project info, and environment overview.
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. - figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.
I'll run the session start ritual.

cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
echo "######## A. REMOTE BRANCHES WITH NO LOCAL BRANCH ########"
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:strip=3)' refs/remotes/origin | grep -v '^HEAD$' | sort > /tmp/_rem.txt
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:strip=2)' refs/heads | sort > /tmp/_loc.txt
# also collect what each local branch tracks, so a differently-named local still counts
git for-each-ref --format='%(upstream:strip=3)' refs/heads | grep -v '^$' | sort -u > /tmp/_tracked.txt
comm -23 /tmp/_rem.txt /tmp/_tracked.txt | while read b; do echo "  MISSING LOCALLY: $b"; done
echo "  (none above = every origin branch is represented locally)"
echo
echo "######## B. LOCAL BRANCH SYNC STATUS ########"
printf "%-58s %-12s %s\n" "BRANCH" "STATE" "DETAIL"
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:strip=2)%09%(upstream:strip=2)' refs/heads | while IFS=$'\t' read -r br up; do
  if [ -z "$up" ]; then printf "  %-56s %-12s %s\n" "$br" "NO-UPSTREAM" "local only"; continue; fi
  if ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$up" >/dev/null; then printf "  %-56s %-12s %s\n" "$br" "GONE" "upstream $up deleted on origin"; continue; fi
  counts=$(git rev-list --left-right --count "$up...$br")
  behind=$(echo "$counts" | cut -f1); ahead=$(echo "$counts" | cut -f2)
  if [ "$behind" = 0 ] && [ "$ahead" = 0 ]; then st="IN-SYNC"; d="$up"
  elif [ "$ahead" = 0 ]; then st="BEHIND"; d="behind $behind of $up (fast-forwardable)"
  elif [ "$behind" = 0 ]; then st="AHEAD"; d="ahead $ahead of $up (unpushed)"
  else st="DIVERGED"; d="ahead $ahead / behind $behind of $up"; fi
  printf "  %-56s %-12s %s\n" "$br" "$st" "$d"
done

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild

The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
been named.

**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
way.

**Input:** `- it's hammertime - maximum effort, let's build:

* https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-236
* https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-83
* https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFC-84` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.

## Depth

Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:

| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |

Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
`exhaustive` is.

---

## Phase 0 — position

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.

---

## Phase 1 — gather

Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.

### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
decision that contradicts the description.

Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.

### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`

Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.

Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
that supersedes it.

### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`

The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.

Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.

The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
is stale.

### Codebase

Branch state, and the shape of what is about to be touched.

- Confirm `develop` is current with `origin/develop`.
- For every likely-touched file: tier and owner, from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and
  `protectedFiles.md`. **Never from `.claude/registry/*.md`** — its Tier column is a derived
  heuristic and is wrong in places.
- Call `/audit-tier <path>` for anything you are unsure about. It also returns import blast radius.
- Find the nearest existing pattern. This codebase has strong precedent; matching it is cheaper
  and more reviewable than inventing.
- Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: **PR #64** (ui-kit atom/molecule,
  four-file pattern, co-located recipe, render-slot wiring), **PR #59** (global-chrome component,
  co-located recipe with shared cross-file values), **PR #56** (pure token layer, no component
  change).

Flag: any Tier 1 file in the likely set · high blast radius (a shared file with many consumers) ·
work that crosses squad territory · an existing pattern the story would contradict.

### Figma

- Design System 2026 — `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`
- Zimmermann_Designs — `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Designs`

**Ask for one node URL per variant and per state**, not one per component. If the file-level
links are not enough to resolve the specific component, stop and ask Marcel. Do not guess at
which node the story means, and do not build from a neighbouring node that looks close.

Check:

- **Completeness** — every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled, loading,
  error, empty, success.
- **Currency** — is this design archived or superseded? Triage archived against current before
  anyone builds to it. An archived node that still renders is a trap.
- **Tokenisation** — does every value map to an existing `--zimm-*` token, or is a new token
  being introduced? A new token is Tier 1 and needs the designer.
- **Responsiveness** — frames exist at 402 / 1023 / 1440; breakpoint tokens are 768 / 860 / 1024.
  **The 768–1022 band is unframed**, so anything in it is an inference, not a design.

Two measurement traps that have produced false defects here. Flag a comparison that hits either:

- **Node type decides comparability.** Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, which is not
  comparable to a CSS line box — never file a mismatch from one. FRAMES and INSTANCES report a
  real box and are directly comparable.
- **The two Figma files must never be cross-compared.** The Design System file and the Designs
  file are different sources; a delta between them is not a defect.

**No design is a blocker, not licence to invent.** If the ACs name something Figma does not have,
that is a finding for Marcel — or an explicit **provisional**, labelled as such and carried into
the plan as an assumption. Never fill the gap silently.

These already exist. Call them; do not reimplement them.

1. `/feature-spec` — turns the gathered picture into a scoped implementation plan and emits a

2. `/scope-check` — run it **on that prompt**. It verdicts SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED and rewrites
   risky prompts. This is the highest-leverage gate available; do not skip it.
3. `/audit-tier <path>` — per file, wherever scope-check flags something specific.

Two known traps when calling these:

- `/code-quality` defaults to diffing against **`main`**; `/pr-checklist` diffs against
  **`develop`**. On a feature branch these give different file sets. Always pass explicit scope.
- `/pr-checklist` already calls `/code-quality` internally. Calling both doubles the audit.

need to branch on a result, restate the verdict yourself rather than parsing theirs.

I am pre-build planning three Jira stories and need the exact current state of the codebase surface they touch:

- SFCC-83 "Recently Viewed UI Component (Shared)" — horizontal rail of recently-viewed product tiles on PLP, PDP, Cart.
- SFCC-84 "Recently Viewed - See Full History" — a full page listing all recently viewed items.

   - Everything under `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` — full contents, exports (default vs named, e.g. `CardBaseline`), props surface, what it renders.

   - Full tree of `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` — every atom, molecule, organism that exists today, with the file set in each (index.tsx, *.css.ts, *.stories.tsx, *.test.tsx).

4. ROUTING (for SFCC-84's new page):
   - `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — full structure, how a route + lazy-loaded page is registered, existing page examples under `overrides/app/pages/`.
   - Is there an existing account/wishlist page pattern to copy?

5. PAGES that would consume these:
   - `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`, any PLP page, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, cart page — do they exist as overrides or only in base? Which currently render product tiles, and how?

6. TIER CLASSIFICATION — read `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` and tell me the tier + owner for every path you named above. Do NOT use `.claude/registry/*.md`.

7. BLAST RADIUS — for `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` and any shared component you'd touch: who imports it? Count and list importers in BOTH `overrides/` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`.

8. CODEOWNERS — read `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS` and report the owning team(s) for each path above.

Be concrete and exhaustive. I need to plan a real build off this, so guessing is worse than saying "not found".

Context: Zimmermann is building a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (www.zimmermann.com). Confluence space key is likely "SFCC". I am pre-build planning three Jira stories and need to know what documentation exists that bears on them, and whether any of it contradicts the tickets.

The three stories:
- SFCC-236 "Product Card Shared Component" — ONE shared product card component with display variations (Homepage, PLP, Wishlist, Recently Viewed Full History) driven by a style prop. Labels: PRC-09, SPR-01, SPR-02, SPR-10..SPR-16, Squad-A. Epic SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components".
- SFCC-83 "Recently Viewed UI Component (Shared)" — horizontal rail of recently-viewed product tiles, surfaces PLP/PDP/Cart. Guest = session-only storage; authenticated = cross-session, cross-device, stored against the customer account. Labels: PRD-027, SPR-61, DesignDependent. Epic SFCC-7 "Search & Recommendations".
- SFCC-84 "Recently Viewed - See Full History" — the page behind the "See Full History" link. Labels: PRD-027, SPR-61, DesignDependent. Epic SFCC-7.

Search Confluence for and REPORT ON:
1. Any TSD (Technical Solution Design) covering product card / product tile / shared components / recently viewed / browsing history. Note the official TSD parent page is 392888324 — check its children.

4. Anything on component reuse / component library / design system / atomic structure (atoms-molecules-organisms) that governs how a shared component should be built.
5. Anything on PLP or Homepage or Wishlist UI that specifies product tile contents.
6. Any page about consent gating that would apply to browsing history (Didomi).

For EVERY page you find, report: page title, page ID, last-updated date, and a tight summary of what it says that is relevant. CRITICALLY: flag any place where the Confluence documentation CONTRADICTS the ticket summaries above, or describes an approach that sounds different from what the tickets describe.

If you find NOTHING for a given topic, say so explicitly and clearly — "no TSD exists for X" is a first-class finding I need, not a failure. Do not pad with irrelevant pages.

content.content:
### 3. Component structure

#### Placement — settled

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.

**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.

#### Tier is by composition, not visual size

Read it off the imports, not the DOM:

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
  come from the caller).
- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
  + local validation state.
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
  owns the subscribe state machine.

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
children don't count.

**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.

#### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always

Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
string key, so this is purely organisational.

The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.

**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).

`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.

#### No data-fetching in `components/`

Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.

**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,
`useUiCopy`) may be called from any component including presentational leaves, because they
read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for
every consumer regardless of route, not anything that varies per page.

**Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades:
`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, one line, renders with zero setup. **`useIntl`
throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the base SFCC `_app`,
not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer
must wrap it.

#### Two API patterns worth copying

- **Encode the a11y contract in a discriminated union** so an inaccessible combination doesn't
  type-check.
- **Make an absent affordance opt-in**, not a silent default.

#### Do not trust the registry's tier column

`generateRegistry.mjs:133-215` hardcodes tier arrays (`TIER1_PATHS` at `:133`, `TIER2_PATHS`
at `:148`, squads at `:178`/`:192`), lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to
Tier 4. The registry is auto-generated and its *paths* are reliable; its
*tier* column is not.

#### What is actually overridden today [CORRECTED]

An earlier revision said **seven** directories. It is now **eleven**:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

`footer/` is a full override with three co-located recipes. Two organisms exist
(`zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmSubscribeSection`) where an earlier note said none did.
`theme/components/button.ts` no longer exists — it is
`ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`. `theme/components/` now holds only
`footerShared.ts`, `header.ts`, `index.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts`,
`recipeGuards.test.ts`.

Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
**Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's worked example not to exist.

---

content.content:
### 7. Building against absent data

#### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

#### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

#### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

#### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

---

### 8. CMS data and the tier reality

@@@@@@@@@@ PLAY 1 @@@@@@@@@@
### Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

Four rungs: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and
needs justification.

**Where to look:** `.claude/registry/` for `Origin` (`Custom` / `Override` / **`Base`**), then
`ui-kits/`. ⚠️ The registry's `Tier` column is unreliable — `generateRegistry.mjs:133-215`
hardcodes tiers, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything to Tier 4.

**`Origin = Base` is the hidden cost.** It means copy-first: mirror the file, convert to TS,
verify the override renders, *then* build. That's real effort and it belongs in the estimate.
Eight components referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` are still base.

**The `shared/ui` barrel exception.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate styling into
base cart/checkout/account looks like enormous leverage. It intercepts nothing — the barrel
re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite, and 212 base files import the barrel
(195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. Don't scope a story around it.

**Duplicate atoms are a human problem.** No tool detects "this is a second Button." The fix
that makes it self-service is one line in the BA's story template: *name the component, and
state whether it exists.*

#### The atoms governance model — decided

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
```

Tier by composition (what the component's own template renders), camelCase for
Zimmermann-authored, a registered recipe always.

⚠️ **The rules set is split on this.** `components.md` and `conventions.md` contain **zero**
occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29`
still scaffolds to the flat path. `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself. Reconciling this
is a standing item.

---

### Play 2 — Estimation validation

**The re-baseline to say once:** pages go *down*, components go *up by more*. Component-based
decomposition front-loads the work.

Split component-build effort from page-composition effort in every estimate. They have
different risk profiles and different owners.

Challenge list:

1. Is it `Origin = Base`? Add copy-first.
2. Does it exist in `ui-kits` already?
3. Is a Contentful content type needed? That's a second story.
4. Is the Figma frame signed off, or "Not Confirmed"?
5. Does it depend on an integration that isn't wired? Most aren't.
6. Does its data exist on the tiers it must demo on?
7. Is it multi-site? Eight storefronts, eleven locales, by default.

---

### Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review

**Configuration variant** (a prop) vs **composition variant** (a container or slot —
structurally a second component). Getting this wrong at story time produces a component that
can't express what the design needs.

### 7. Building against absent data

#### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

#### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

#### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

#### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

---

### 8. CMS data and the tier reality

@@@@@@@@@@ PLAY 1 @@@@@@@@@@
### Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

Four rungs: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and
needs justification.

**Where to look:** `.claude/registry/` for `Origin` (`Custom` / `Override` / **`Base`**), then
`ui-kits/`. ⚠️ The registry's `Tier` column is unreliable — `generateRegistry.mjs:133-215`
hardcodes tiers, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything to Tier 4.

**`Origin = Base` is the hidden cost.** It means copy-first: mirror the file, convert to TS,
verify the override renders, *then* build. That's real effort and it belongs in the estimate.
Eight components referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` are still base.

**The `shared/ui` barrel exception.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate styling into
base cart/checkout/account looks like enormous leverage. It intercepts nothing — the barrel
re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite, and 212 base files import the barrel
(195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. Don't scope a story around it.

**Duplicate atoms are a human problem.** No tool detects "this is a second Button." The fix
that makes it self-service is one line in the BA's story template: *name the component, and
state whether it exists.*

#### The atoms governance model — decided

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
```

Tier by composition (what the component's own template renders), camelCase for
Zimmermann-authored, a registered recipe always.

⚠️ **The rules set is split on this.** `components.md` and `conventions.md` contain **zero**
occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29`
still scaffolds to the flat path. `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself. Reconciling this
is a standing item.

### Play 2 — Estimation validation

**The re-baseline to say once:** pages go *down*, components go *up by more*. Component-based
decomposition front-loads the work.

Split component-build effort from page-composition effort in every estimate. They have
different risk profiles and different owners.

Challenge list:

1. Is it `Origin = Base`? Add copy-first.
2. Does it exist in `ui-kits` already?
3. Is a Contentful content type needed? That's a second story.
4. Is the Figma frame signed off, or "Not Confirmed"?
5. Does it depend on an integration that isn't wired? Most aren't.

content.content:
################ search.md §7.4 ################
### 7.2 Recommendation Logic (SPR-59, Confirmed)

- Mix of AI-driven and rules-gated recommendation logic, configurable by season and category (reflecting current SearchSpring behaviour carried forward).

### 7.3 "Complete the Look" / "Shop the Look" Cross-Sell (SPR-60, Confirmed)

- Cross-sell surface on PDP, Cart, and slide-out Mini-Bag — configurable through SFCC.
- *Open: additional surfaces TBC. Whether "Shop the Look" is PDP-only and "You May Also Like" covers other touchpoints pending design.*

### 7.4 "Recently Viewed" (SPR-61, Confirmed)

- Carousel shown on PDP and Cart.
- Browsing history stored in browser session; persisted cross-session on login.
- Current display shows thumbnail image only (no product name or price) — dependent on new designs.
- *Open: additional surfaces from Work & Co redesigns (PLP, Find in Boutique, Z.Immerse) are TBC — do not implement on those surfaces until confirmed.*

### 7.5 Add to Bag from Recommendation Carousels (SPR-62, Confirmed)

- Add to Bag via size variant selection directly from recommendation carousels on PDP and Cart pages.
- Whether the affordance is Add to Bag or Add to Wishlist is a customisation decision (IC 2026-05-25).

45:- Contentful is the sole CMS across all regional storefronts (HPC-001, confirmed). Integration is via the Salesforce App Exchange connector, consuming content through the Contentful delivery API for all customer-facing pages (Third Party Integrations — CMS / Contentful). Homepage carries product names only, which sit in Contentful.
51:- **Editorial modules**: campaign imagery, collection features, product spotlights (HPC-009, confirmed)
58:- **Contentful vs SFCC scope split** (HPC-001, HPC-002, HPC-006, HPC-010, HPC-012) — pending discussion with Contentful. Affects whether product names/prices sit in Contentful or SFCC ("EK - If we are displaying Product names and Potentially prices this would sit on SFCC").

############ account.md — Wishlist section ############
- The following are **global** (shared across all storefronts): Orders, Returns, Wishlist, Address Book, Communication Preferences (CRM-172)
- **Saved cards** (CRM-173): Adyen tokens are stored globally at the customer level, but only cards saved via domestic orders are displayed. Cards captured through Global-e international checkouts are **not** saved to SFCC or Adyen
- **Omneo** is the system of record for customer identity and loyalty. SFCC ↔ Omneo sync via MuleSoft

---

## 2. Registration & Login (CRM-001 – CRM-016)

### Login (CRM-001–003, all Confirmed)
- **CRM-001:** Login page with email + password, authenticated against SFCC. SSO (Apple/Google) is **not yet in scope** — the sheet defers it to the ENH tab pending further discussion; treat as Open until confirmed (see Open Items).
- **CRM-002:** Email + password validated against SFCC on submission. Currently unlimited login attempts; SFCC OOTB supports a 3-attempt lockout or a custom value — **decision pending on the lockout threshold**.
- **CRM-003:** Password reset directs the customer to a dedicated Reset Password page; the customer must re-enter their email to initiate the flow. Email pre-fill is **not** OOTB and not recommended for security (05.05) — implementation will follow the OOTB pattern unless explicitly overridden. On login, an incorrect password must be handled gracefully with a clear error message (VR/RT comment).

### Registration (CRM-004–011, all Confirmed)
- **CRM-004:** Registration form fields: First Name, Last Name, Email Address, Mobile Number (with country prefix), Password, Confirm Password. Mobile is optional on all storefronts. Mandatory mobile for ME has been **removed** (IC 2026-05-06). ME currently has a "title" field in the form; any further ME-specific field variation is TBC and will be revisited as part of the forms improvement project — **do not implement ME-only fields beyond title until confirmed**.
- **CRM-005:** Email validated against existing SFCC records at registration. If an account exists → prompt to log in or reset. If a Boutique/Omneo account exists but a password has never been created → show a "create a password" flow (not "reset"), encouraging the customer to set a password to surface known Omneo data. Requires customisation, not OOTB.
- **CRM-006:** Password complexity rules enforced at creation and reset.
- **CRM-007:** Optional marketing opt-in checkbox at registration — label: *"Discover new arrivals, exclusive offers and personalised experiences"*. On success, preference passed to Omneo; welcome email triggered via Emarsys. See also Marketing Opt-In (CRM-178–179).
- **CRM-008:** Google reCAPTCHA on login and registration pages.
- **CRM-009:** Link to Privacy Policy relevant to the customer's storefront shown at point of registration.
- **CRM-010:** Customer record created in SFCC on successful registration; immediate bidirectional sync to Omneo via webhook.
- **CRM-011:** Bidirectional sync maintained between SFCC and Omneo — updates in either system reflect in the other.
- **CRM-016:** Show/hide password toggle on all password entry fields.

### Magento migration note
**Passwords were NOT migrated from Magento** — all existing customers must reset at go-live (CFD-013). Plan for a comms email at launch.

### Guest account / Omneo record creation (CRM-012–015, all Confirmed — but conflict pending resolution)

The spreadsheet rows are marked Confirmed, but the TT and IC comments are in tension and legal review remains open. Treat as **Open** for implementation until reconciled (see Open Items):

- **CRM-012:** Per TT, an Omneo record is created when a customer begins guest checkout, regardless of marketing opt-in. IC counter-position: SFCC best practice (record at order completion only) should be implemented. Conflict unresolved.
- **CRM-013:** Where marketing opt-in is **not** ticked, the Omneo record is created with first/last name set to `unknown` and the email as identifier; name updates if the order completes. My Account must never display "unknown" — fall back to hiding the "Hi [name]" greeting when no name is available.
- **CRM-014:** Where the marketing opt-in checkbox **is** ticked, the Omneo record is created with opted-in marketing status (consistent with footer newsletter behaviour).
- **CRM-015:** Customer address and remaining order details populated in Omneo upon order completion.

See also **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** — Omneo guest record creation timing.

---

## 3. My Account Sections

### Dashboard (CRM-017–029)

All dashboard items are **Confirmed**.

content.text:
Verified independently — the sweep was right, and it changes the shape of this build. Confluence is still running; here's what's already settled.

## The thing that matters most

**SFCC-236 has no foundation to build on.** `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` does not exist. Neither does `CardBaseline` — it appears exactly three times in the repo, all of them prose in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (lines 128, 181, 186), describing a file and an export that have never been written. Zero occurrences in any `.ts`/`.tsx`.

Worth naming: the skill told me that where `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` disagrees with `overrideStyling.md`, **the rules file wins**. Here that precedence rule points the wrong way — the handbook correctly lists `product-tile` as still-base, and the rules file is the stale one. I checked the filesystem rather than trusting either.

**And there's a live trap in the obvious approach.** The moment `overrides/app/components/product-tile/index.tsx` exists, the overrides resolver silently redirects every base import to it — PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results all change with no edit to any of them. Worse:

```
import ProductTile, {
    Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile'
```

That's `pages/product-list/index.jsx:51-53`. An override missing a named `Skeleton` export **breaks PLP at import time**. Building the card in `ui-kits/` instead keeps the blast radius to files that explicitly import it.

## Three more that change scope

- **Recently Viewed has no data source.** Zero hits for `recentlyViewed`/`browsingHistory` across overrides, `retail-react-app`, and `commerce-sdk-react`. No SFCC API. The only thing that exists is the Einstein recommender string `viewed-recently-einstein` — which your PDP override already renders at `product-detail/index.tsx:1007`. So SFCC-83 on PDP is a *replacement*, and SFCC-84's "full history" is something Einstein structurally cannot return.
- **Three of SFCC-236's four surfaces have no page override** — PLP, Cart and Wishlist are all base-only. And base Wishlist renders `ProductItem` (a row), not a card at all.
- **Your own PRDs contradict the ACs.** `plp.md §2.5` (SPR-14, Confirmed) and `account.md` CRM-113 both require a **save-to-wishlist icon on every tile**. SFCC-236 is *labelled* SPR-14 — but no AC mentions it. Separately, `search.md §7.4` says Recently Viewed is **PDP and Cart**, and explicitly lists PLP under *"do not implement on those surfaces until confirmed"* — while SFCC-83 names PLP as a confirmed surface.

## Sprint reality

All three are in **SFCC Sprint 4**, which ends **7 Sep** — five days. SFCC-236 is 8 points, SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 are 2 each. For calibration, PR #64 (SFCC-89, static product info — no variants, no hover states, no new page) was **43 files**.

## What I need from you

The Figma gate is still the hard blocker. Concretely, to unblock SFCC-236 I need node URLs for:

| Variation | States needed |
|---|---|
| PLP | default · desktop hover · out-of-stock · mobile |
| Homepage | default · desktop hover · mobile |
| Wishlist | default · desktop hover |
| Recently Viewed Full History | default · desktop hover · mobile |
| **Recently Viewed rail** (SFCC-83) | default — **no rail component exists in the DS at all**, only a tile-level `Recently Viewed Product` |
| **See Full History page** (SFCC-84) | page frame — desktop + mobile |

I'll fold in the Confluence findings and put the full gate table in front of you as soon as that sweep returns. Nothing gets planned or built until you've seen it.
